name: wake-slider
title: Wake Slider
description: A horizontal volume control drawn as a row of slim vertical bars. Bars up to the value glow white, and dragging faster lifts the bars around the handle into a short wave that settles when you stop.
use: An audio, brightness or any 0-100 control wants a more tactile readout than a plain track and knob.
avoid: The wake only shows mid-drag, and on touch the narrow bars make precise values fiddly.
a11y: A hidden slider button makes every key work and exposes value text, but it has no visible focus ring. (keyboard: yes, labels: good, reduced motion: respected)
looks: A dark rounded card holds a small title and subtitle above a single row of about thirty evenly spaced rounded bars. Filled bars are pale grey and the rest sit dim, with a percentage at the right.
behaves: Clicking or dragging anywhere on the bar row sets the level, and the lit bars follow the pointer. Moving quickly lifts neighbouring bars into a peaked wake that flattens as the drag slows.
customise: Value, min, max, step, bar count, height, gaps, colours, sensitivity, wake reach and skew are props; the label format is a function prop.
weight: light: 32 CSS-transformed bars updated by springs only while the value moves.
